```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.5)
```

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(herminR)
```

MPI rankings depend on which terms survive model selection (referee W5).
`mpi_selection_paths()` runs backward elimination along an AIC path and
partial-F paths at several significance levels. It works on individual
monomial terms, even for `rsm` `SO()` fits, and by default keeps the
polynomial well formed (a main effect stays while its square or an interaction
containing it remains).

```{r}
data(pastrydough)
fit <- lm(y ~ block + (x1 + x2 + x3)^2 + I(x1^2) + I(x2^2) + I(x3^2),
          data = pastrydough)
sp <- mpi_selection_paths(fit, alphas = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.10), top = 1)
sp
lapply(attr(sp, "paths"), `[[`, "terms")
plot(sp)
```

A factor whose terms are all removed on a path stays in the table with MPI 0.
`stability` is the fraction of paths on which the factor ranks within `top`.
This is a sensitivity analysis over a few plausible procedures, not a test.
